newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil, Chile to talk about defense policies.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, Chile to talk about defense policies.

text.p: Brazil and Chile said on Monday they will hold talks on military issues to help reduce the risk of an arms race in South America.

After meeting his Chilean counterpart Jose Miguel Insulza, Brazilian Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia said similar talks between Brazil and Argentina had improved understanding of each country's military modernisation programmes.
"Minister Insulza and I discussed the possibility of having a similar consultation mechanism for military coordination," Lampreia told a news conference.
Insulza said the discussions might begin "within the next few months" and would help deepen military cooperation within South America.
He said Chile's plan to purchase between 16 and 18 high performance fighter aircraft did not pose a threat to the region's stability.

"I don't think anyone can say that this will start an arms race...There is another South American country that bought a sigficantly larger number recently without anyone raising the alarm," Insulza said.

Peru bought at least 12 MiG-29 fighter jets from Belarus earlier this year, raising fears of a regional arms race. Such fears gained ground when U.S. President Bill Clinton lifted a 20-year ban on advanced weapons sales to Latin America this month.
Insulza, in Brazil for talks on range of issues including trade, played down the concerns, saying the U.S. decision was a positive one that reflected the end of military dictatorship in the region.
